o: Letting an app access a user's resources without their password
Proving the owner of a website's identity
Storing user passwords safely in the browser
v.w: OAuth 2.0 is a delegated authorization framework. Login (who is this user?) is added by OpenID Connect on top.

v.q: Which statement about OAuth 2.0 is NOT true?
o: It lets an app collect the user password
It avoids sharing the password with the client
v.w: OAuth exists so the client never sees the user password.

v.q: Which grant type should a server-side web app or SPA use for user login in a modern setup?
v.w: The implicit and password grants are discouraged in OAuth 2.1. Authorization Code with PKCE keeps tokens out of the URL and protects the code from interception.

v.q: Which grant is no longer recommended for browser apps?
v.w: The implicit grant returns tokens in the URL. Use the authorization code flow with PKCE instead.

v.q: Which grant fits a backend service calling another service with no user involved?
v.w: The service authenticates itself with its own credentials and gets an access token for machine-to-machine calls.

v.q: Which grant fits a nightly batch job that calls an API as itself?
v.w: There is no user, so the service authenticates with its own client id and secret.

o: It binds the code to the requesting client, so a stolen code fails
It encrypts the access token while it sits in the browser
It refreshes tokens without making any network call
It hides the client id from the person using the app
v.w: The client sends a hashed code challenge up front and the verifier when exchanging the code. An attacker who intercepts the code does not have the verifier.

v.q: Which statement about PKCE is NOT true?
o: It replaces the need for HTTPS
It sends a code challenge in the first request
It sends a code verifier when redeeming the code
v.w: PKCE protects the code exchange but HTTPS is still required.

v.q: Who are the four roles in OAuth 2.0?
o: Resource owner, client, authorization server and resource server
User, browser, database and firewall in the request path
Issuer, subject, audience and verifier of a token claim
Producer, consumer, broker and registry of a message bus
v.w: The owner is the user. The client is the app. The authorization server issues tokens. The resource server hosts the API that accepts them.

v.q: Which party issues the access token?
v.w: The authorization server authenticates the user, gets consent and issues tokens. The resource server only checks them.

v.q: What is the `state` parameter in the authorization request used for?
o: It guards against CSRF by matching the response to the request
It stores the user's session on the server
It tells the server which scopes to remove
It chooses the lifetime of the token
v.w: The client generates an unpredictable value, sends it, and checks that the same value comes back in the redirect.

v.q: An attacker sends a victim a link containing the attacker authorization code. Which parameter helps reject it?
v.w: The client checks that the state in the response matches the one it created for this request.

o: The specific permissions the client asks for, such as read-only access
The lifetime of the token, measured in minutes or hours
The list of servers that a token is allowed to reach
The encryption algorithm that is used to protect the token
v.w: Scopes limit what a token can do. Grant the least access needed, and let the resource server check them.

v.q: A client asks for the scope read:accounts. What may it do?
v.w: A scope limits the token to the permissions the user consented to.

v.q: Why must the redirect URI be registered and compared exactly by the authorization server?
o: An attacker could get the code or token sent to their own site
It makes the redirect itself a little quicker
It lets the user pick any site to return to
Browsers need it before they will store cookies
v.w: Open or loosely matched redirect URIs are a classic way to steal authorization codes.

v.q: Which registered redirect URI rule is correct?
o: Any URI on the same host
v.w: Loose matching lets an attacker steer the code to a page they control.
